pos.personaBrief: Guardiola: 'We want possession for as long as possible' (2011) and 'the best way to defend is to attack well' (2009); StatsBomb notes long sequences of controlled possession in the 2009 final.

pro.personaBrief: Centre-backs play into midfielders' feet and the team plays out from the back under pressure using technical superiority (2011 final, 2011/12 Athletic); 'retaining possession and quick interchange of passes' is a core trait, with Busquets dropping between the centre-backs.

est.personaBrief: Positional play with wide forwards holding high and wide positions (Henry on the touchline 2009; Pedro and Villa 2011) and rational occupation of space, combined with a false nine who drops close to Xavi and a 4-3-3 that becomes 3-4-3.

lar.personaBrief: Width is used to pin full-backs and stretch the pitch (Henry/Eto'o, Pedro/Villa high and wide, Alves overlapping), but the goal route runs through the middle via Messi, Xavi and Iniesta with no proper striker, not via crosses.

blo.personaBrief: 'Intense pressing high up the opposition's half' is the trademark, Guardiola 'ordered his team to press very high' (2011/12), a high line is played and the counter-press produced the third goal in the 2011 final.

mar.personaBrief: Space-based positional defending with a high line and Touré covering spaces, though the press on the opponent's build-up became nearly man-oriented in one 2011/12 match; corner marking is not verified and comes from general knowledge.

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence on game-management (gap axis); from general knowledge Guardiola imposed a fixed game model and kept it against any opponent, adjusting shapes (3-4-3, 4-2-4) by detail, consistent with 'in the end our football won the day'.

res.personaBrief: A Cruyffian side that attacked to defend and sought possession to create as many attacking situations as possible, while winning 14 trophies; it played to win away and did not shut games down.

sis.personaBrief: A highly drilled collective where everyone presses, Messi included as the false nine with a defined role, and stars judged on performance ('si estuvieran a su nivel, estarían con nosotros'), though built around Messi's talent.

jog.personaBrief: Technical superiority to play in tight spaces, midfielders used as centre-backs (Touré, Mascherano) and a small technical midfield of Xavi, Iniesta, Busquets define the team.

bas.personaBrief: Nine academy products started the 2011 Club World Cup final; young players like Busquets and Pedro were promoted straight into a title-winning XI.

lid.personaBrief: Little verified evidence (gap axis): only the pre-period June 2008 decision to plan without Ronaldinho, Deco and Eto'o for performance and 'less tangible' reasons; from general knowledge Guardiola was a demanding authority who protected group unity and treated stars by the same rules.
